## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
No trials have run yet. The starting architecture scored 0.000 on both seeds. With the default recipe it gets only about 32 PPO updates of 4,096 steps, which is very few for a task that needs exact builds. From the code: the observation is [B, 4Z+3, Y, X] with layers as channels. Actions are laid out type-major (t·Y·X + y·X + x, anchor at the top-left cell) with DONE last, and footprints come from spec. The plan for this round is a 2x2 comparison of two factors. Candidate 1 changes only the recipe (2 epochs, higher gamma and lambda, lower entropy) on the starting network. Candidate 2 adds a new fully convolutional residual network with a footprint-shaped spatial head, at about the same compute, under that same recipe. Candidate 3 is candidate 2 with 1 PPO epoch, which roughly doubles the number of environment steps. If every trial scores 0 on dev, I will compare them by training success.

### Round 2
All three round-1 trials, and the starting network, scored exactly 0 on dev and 0 on training success. Changing the network, using 1 or 2 epochs, or getting about 1.75x more samples made no measurable difference. The common factor is optimisation volume. With 4096-sample updates and 128-sample minibatches, each trial made only about 55–95 policy updates and about 3,000–3,600 gradient steps. That is very little for PPO on a precise multi-step task. Compute counts samples × epochs, not optimiser steps. So minibatches of 64 samples and 1024-sample updates give about 4x more PPO iterations and about 2x more gradient steps at the same compute. This round tests that recipe on the round-1 ResNet with 2 epochs and with 4 epochs. A third candidate pairs it with a footprint-pooling network that has a deeper per-cell stem and takes the action mask as input.

### Round 3
All six trials score exactly 0 on dev and 0 on training success, across two head designs, 1 to 4 PPO epochs, 64 to 256 envs and up to 389k steps. Tuning the recipe or adding small inductive biases changed nothing measurable, so the cause is probably structural, not noise. Every network so far has a spatial head that assumes action index = type*Y*X + y*X + x, with the anchor at the top-left. The task warns that this world may differ from its description. If the real action layout is transposed, cell-major or uses a different anchor, local conv heads cannot learn the mapping, and that would explain zero training success. This round tests that directly: (1) a layout-agnostic flat linear head, (2) the spatial head with its output transposed, (3) a hybrid of the conv head and the flat head. The recipe is held fixed so the three results can be compared.

### Round 4
All 9 trials scored exactly 0, on dev and in training, across every seed. The recipe changes made no difference: epochs 1, 2 and 4, batch sizes, and 54 to 216 updates all scored 0. The head layouts made no difference either: footprint conv, transposed, flat linear and hybrid all scored 0. So a wrong action layout is unlikely to be the cause, and more samples or more updates alone do not help. Two causes remain plausible.

1. **Representation.** A valid placement needs a learned choice of layer: the landing layer is the highest build cell under the footprint, and the footprint cells must be missing at that layer. Flat-channel 2D networks find this hard.
2. **Early collapse.** Random placements cost reward, so the agent may learn to call DONE early, or stop exploring.

This is the last round, nothing beats the start, and all three trials score 0, so big changes are justified. Two candidates test a network that shares weights across layers, pools over brick footprints and takes a soft maximum over layers. One tests the collapse idea with a much higher entropy coefficient.
